items.headline: Workers' Party to hold special cadres conference on 28 June over Pritam Singh's future
items.summary: Workers' Party cadres will vote on whether secretary-general Pritam Singh should remain in his role at a special conference on 28 June, triggered by a requisition signed by 25 cadres. Singh was convicted in December 2025 of lying to a parliamentary select committee; he faces a secret ballot unless he steps down voluntarily beforehand.

items.headline: NParks to relocate Singapore's last wild cats — five leopard cats in Changi — from H2 2026
items.summary: The National Parks Board confirmed five leopard cats living in Changi's coastal forest and will move them to other nature areas from the second half of 2026. Fewer than 20 individuals are believed to remain on the Singapore mainland, making the species locally critically endangered.

items.headline: Singapore life expectancy rises to record 83.9 years in 2025, narrowing gap with Japan
items.summary: Data from the Department of Statistics shows residents born in 2025 can expect to live 83.9 years on average, up 0.2 years from 2024, placing Singapore level with Japan for the world's longest lifespans.

items.headline: IMD issues orange alert as pre-monsoon storms bring heavy rain and lightning to seven states
items.summary: The India Meteorological Department warned of widespread thunderstorms and lightning across Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Vidarbha on 5 June. The Southwest Monsoon has advanced into parts of Kerala ahead of schedule.

items.headline: Shubman Gill named India Test captain for one-off match against Afghanistan in New Chandigarh
items.summary: The BCCI has handed Shubman Gill his first red-ball captaincy for the five-day Test against Afghanistan starting Saturday at Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium. Jasprit Bumrah and Ravindra Jadeja have been rested; KL Rahul is named vice-captain.

items.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree to conditional ceasefire; Hezbollah rejects the terms and vows to fight on
items.summary: Israel and Lebanon announced a conditional truce centred on Hezbollah withdrawing north of the Litani River. Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected the deal on Thursday, calling it 'a roadmap to annihilate part of the Lebanese people' and pledging to continue attacks while Israeli forces remain on Lebanese soil.

items.headline: US-Iran peace talks stall as both sides exchange strikes; Hormuz shipping stays at a fraction of normal
items.summary: Iranian negotiators stopped messaging US intermediaries this week, vowing to completely block the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for ceasefire violations, while US forces and Iranian forces exchanged missile and drone strikes near Qeshm Island. Only around seven ships transited the strait on Friday, compared with roughly 100 vessels a day before February.

items.headline: Wired finds dormant facial-recognition pipeline — code-named NameTag — embedded in Meta's AI app
items.summary: Code distributed to millions of phones captures faces via Ray-Ban smart glasses, converts them into biometric data, and is designed to identify acquaintances in real time, Wired reported after a security researcher reviewed the Meta AI app. No part of NameTag is currently live, but more than 70 civil liberties groups have demanded Meta abandon the feature.

items.headline: Trump signs narrower AI executive order asking companies to voluntarily submit frontier models for pre-release review
items.summary: The order asks AI developers to give the US government up to 30 days of early access to their most powerful models for national security and cybersecurity assessment. An earlier 90-day-window draft was softened after industry pushback; participation is explicitly voluntary.

items.headline: Broadcom falls 15% as Q3 AI chip revenue guidance of $16bn misses Wall Street's $17.2bn estimate
items.summary: Shares in Broadcom (AVGO) dropped roughly 15% after CEO Hock Tan gave a Q3 AI semiconductor revenue target that fell $1.2 billion short of analyst consensus, despite Q2 AI revenue doubling year-on-year to $10.8 billion. The full-year $100 billion AI chip target was left unchanged.

items.headline: Brent eases below $97 on Israel-Lebanon ceasefire hopes, but Hormuz blockade keeps oil elevated
items.summary: Front-month Brent fell roughly 1% on Thursday on diplomatic progress in Lebanon that briefly raised hopes for a broader Iran deal. Prices remain more than 30% above pre-conflict levels; Bloomberg noted the blockade-for-blockade standoff is the central sticking point in US-Iran negotiations.

items.headline: RBI holds repo rate at 5.25% for third consecutive meeting, citing Iran-war inflation risk
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India's MPC voted unanimously to leave the benchmark rate at 5.25%, the third straight hold. Governor Malhotra cited the Strait of Hormuz closure as raising FY27 inflation risks and lifted the CPI forecast to 5.1% from 4.6%; GDP growth guidance was kept at 6.6%.

items.headline: Mirra Andreeva beats Kostyuk 6-1, 6-3 to reach first Grand Slam final at Roland Garros
items.summary: The 19-year-old Russian, seeded eighth, dominated in 76 minutes on Thursday, ending Kostyuk's 17-match winning streak. Andreeva will face Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska in Saturday's final.

items.headline: George Russell snatches Canadian GP pole from team-mate Antonelli with final-lap effort; Mercedes lock out front row
items.summary: Russell posted a 1:12.578 with his final flying lap at Circuit Gilles Villeneuve to edge Kimi Antonelli by 0.068 seconds, ending the Italian rookie's run of three consecutive sprint-qualifying poles. Lando Norris qualified third; Lewis Hamilton placed fifth for Ferrari.

items.headline: Pakistan hold nerve to beat Australia by four wickets, clinch ODI series 2-1 in Lahore
items.summary: Chasing 158 in the series decider at Gaddafi Stadium, Pakistan scraped home in 41.5 overs as Shadab Khan's unbeaten 29 off 42 balls guided a nervy chase. Australia had been bowled out for 157, with Shaheen Shah Afridi taking three wickets.

fun_fact.headline: Mantis shrimp have 16 types of photoreceptor cells compared to three in humans
fun_fact.body: Mantis shrimp have 16 types of colour-photoreceptor cells — compared to just three in human eyes — yet laboratory tests show they are surprisingly poor at distinguishing similar shades. Scientists believe they 'sample' colour at each point in space rather than comparing hues across the field of view, trading fine colour discrimination for near-instant processing speed.
fun_fact.source: Royal Society Biology Letters (Thoen et al., 2014); also confirmed in Smithsonian Magazine

puzzle.body: Three boxes are mislabelled. Box 1 says 'Apples', Box 2 says 'Oranges', Box 3 says 'Apples and Oranges'. All three labels are wrong. You may pick exactly one fruit from exactly one box without looking inside first. Which box do you pick from, and how does that single pick let you correctly label all three boxes?
puzzle.approach: Focus on the most constrained box — if all labels are wrong, what are the only possible contents of the 'Apples and Oranges' box?
puzzle.answer: Pick from Box 3. Since all labels are wrong, it cannot be mixed — it's either all-Apples or all-Oranges. If you draw an apple: Box 3 = Apples; Box 1 (labelled Apples) cannot be Apples or Mixed (if Mixed, Box 2 = Oranges = label correct, contradiction), so Box 1 = Oranges and Box 2 = Mixed. Mirror logic if you draw an orange.
